questions.question: When the web page calls a Rust function from JavaScript, how does that call physically travel from the webview into Rust and how does the result come back?
questions.answerNote: invoke() in @tauri-apps/api calls window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke; the injected ipc-protocol.js POSTs the payload with fetch to the ipc:// custom protocol (headers Tauri-Callback, Tauri-Error, Tauri-Invoke-Key). ipc/protocol.rs parses the request, checks the invoke key and dispatches to the webview's command handler; the HTTP response body resolves the callback via runCallback. If the custom protocol fails (CSP, Android) it falls back to window.ipc.postMessage handled by the same message_handler, replying by evaluating JS.

questions.question: How does the app decide whether a particular window is allowed to call a given backend command?
questions.answerNote: Capabilities (JSON/TOML files) group permission identifiers and bind them to window/webview labels (globs allowed), platforms, and local or remote URL contexts. At build time they are resolved into an ACL; at runtime RuntimeAuthority::resolve_access (called from webview/mod.rs on each invoke) rejects explicitly denied commands for the origin, then returns the allowed ResolvedCommand only if the origin matches and a window or webview label matches; otherwise the call fails with a 'not allowed' message listing the missing permission.

questions.question: My Rust command takes a parameter called user_id, but the frontend has to send it as userId. Why, and can I change that?
questions.answerNote: The #[command] attribute macro (tauri-macros command/wrapper.rs) generates a wrapper that extracts each argument by key; by default the key is the argument name converted to lower camelCase. #[tauri::command(rename_all = "snake_case")] switches to snake_case keys (rename_all accepts only camelCase or snake_case).

questions.question: How do the built frontend files end up inside the final desktop executable, and how are they served to the webview at runtime?
questions.answerNote: At compile time generate_context!/tauri-build codegen reads build.frontendDist from the config; EmbeddedAssets walks that directory, brotli-compresses each file into OUT_DIR (hash-named, cached), records CSP hashes for inline scripts/styles, and emits include_bytes! for every asset so they are baked into the binary. At runtime the tauri:// protocol handler (protocol/tauri.rs) looks assets up via the manager's get_asset (or proxies to devUrl in dev).

questions.question: Can I keep separate app configuration overrides for macOS and Windows, and which file formats are accepted?
questions.answerNote: The main config is tauri.conf.json (Config struct in tauri-utils config.rs); JSON5 (tauri.conf.json5) and TOML (Tauri.toml) are supported behind the config-json5/config-toml features. Platform files tauri.<linux|windows|macos|android|ios>.conf.json (or Tauri.<platform>.toml) are read by config/parse.rs and merged over the main config.

questions.question: Why are there both an npm package and a Rust crate for the command-line tool, and how are they related?
questions.answerNote: ARCHITECTURE.md: @tauri-apps/cli (packages/cli) is a wrapper around the Rust tauri-cli built with napi-rs to publish per-platform npm packages. packages/cli/src/lib.rs exposes a #[napi] run() that calls tauri_cli::try_run(args) on a separate thread and reports success/failure through a Node threadsafe callback.

questions.question: What is the isolation pattern and how does it protect messages coming from the frontend?
questions.answerNote: With the isolation pattern every IPC message is first sent to a hidden, sandboxed iframe (#__tauri_isolation__) running the app's isolation application; its __TAURI_ISOLATION_HOOK__ can inspect/modify the payload, then isolation.js encrypts it with an AES-GCM key generated at runtime (Web Crypto) before posting it back. pattern/isolation.rs holds the runtime-generated AES-256-GCM keys and decryption; crates/tauri/src/ipc/protocol.rs decrypts the payload before dispatch (protocol/isolation.rs serves the iframe page with CSP), so frontend code cannot forge IPC without going through the hook.

questions.question: When Rust code broadcasts an event, how does it reach a listener that was registered in the page's JavaScript?
questions.answerNote: listen() in @tauri-apps/api/event invokes plugin:event|listen with a transformCallback handler id; Rust records the JS listener per webview/target. On emit, Listeners::emit_js_filter selects webviews with matching JS listeners and Webview::emit_js evals emit_js_script, which calls the injected listeners function that runs each handler via __TAURI_INTERNALS__.runCallback. Rust-side listeners are called directly.
